title: Minimal generators detected after extending a residue field
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m$, let $M$ be an $A$-module generated by finitely many elements, and let $F\to L$ be a homomorphism of fields. Put $V=M/\mathfrak mM$, where $\mathfrak mM$ is the submodule spanned by the elements $am$ with $a\in\mathfrak m$ and $m\in M$, and give $V$ its quotient $F$-vector-space structure. Write $W=V\otimes_FL$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Both $V$ and $W$ are finite dimensional. For every integer $r\geq0$ the following are equivalent: $M$ admits an $A$-generating family indexed by $\{1,\ldots,r\}$; $\dim_FV\leq r$; and $\dim_LW\leq r$. Consequently the least number of generators of $M$ is
$$\dim_FV=\dim_LW.$$
More precisely, for every $F$-basis $(v_i)_{1\leq i\leq d}$ of $V$, any chosen lifts $m_i\in M$ of $v_i$ generate $M$; the vectors $v_i\otimes1$ form an $L$-basis of $W$, and no family of fewer than $d$ elements generates $M$. The same statements hold with $V$ replaced by the canonically isomorphic fibre $M\otimes_AF$, and with $W$ replaced by $M\otimes_AL$. The case $r=d=0$ is included.

Returned step 3(c) basis calculation and step 5 basis lifting.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating list of $M$. Its images span $V$: reduce the coefficients of an $A$-linear expression modulo $\mathfrak m$. Thus $V$ is finite dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Extract a basis from this finite spanning list as follows. Whenever the current list is dependent, choose a relation $\sum a_i v_i=0$ with $a_j\ne0$, and delete $v_j$, since $v_j=-a_j^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}a_iv_i$. Its span is unchanged and its length decreases; termination gives an independent spanning list, hence a basis. By [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] its length is $d=\dim_FV$. The same deletion argument applied to any spanning list of length $r$ shows $d\le r$. The empty list spans precisely the zero space.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), proof, residue-fibre dimension equality and Nakayama paragraph; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), parts (4) and (8).

proof.text: Let $(v_i)_{1\le i\le d}$ be any $F$-basis, and choose arbitrary lifts $m_i\in M$ under the surjective quotient map. Their images span $V$, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] says that the $m_i$ generate $M$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is local and $M$ is finitely generated; it imposes no Noetherian or freeness hypothesis. This also applies to the empty basis.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), proof, residue-fibre dimension equality and Nakayama paragraph; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), parts (4) and (8).

proof.text: If an $r$-element family generates $M$, its images span $V$, so step 1 gives $d\le r$. Conversely, if $d\le r$, append $r-d$ zero elements to the lifts from step 2; the resulting family indexed by $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ still generates $M$. Hence $M$ has such a family exactly when $\dim_FV\le r$, and $d$ is the least possible length. In particular no shorter family generates $M$. For $d=0$, step 2 says $M=0$, and zero padding treats every $r\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), proof, residue-fibre dimension equality and Nakayama paragraph; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), parts (4) and (8).

proof.text: Write $\iota:F\to L$ for the given field map, so $L$ is an $F$-module through $\iota$. The chosen family $(v_i)_{1\le i\le d}$ is a basis of $V$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module] (every $v$ is uniquely $\sum_ip_i(v)v_i$ with $p_i(v)\in F$), so $V$ is a free $F$-module with this basis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] to $R=F$, $A=L$ and the free module $V$ in its second form: $W=V\otimes_FL$ is a free $L$-module with basis $(v_i\otimes1)_{1\le i\le d}$; concretely $v\otimes\ell=\sum_i(v_i\otimes1)\,\iota(p_i(v))\ell$ on the pure tensors, which generate $W$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus the $v_i\otimes1$ are a finite spanning family, so $W$ is finite dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and the basis count of [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives $\dim_LW=d=\dim_FV$. For $d=0$ the basis is empty, so $W=0$. The argument uses no hypothesis on $L/F$ (finite, separable or not).

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), proof, residue-fibre dimension equality and Nakayama paragraph; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), parts (4) and (8).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] to $R=A$, $J=\mathfrak m$, first with the quotient $F$, and then with the $F$-module $L$. Swapping tensor factors by the bilinear map $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$ (its square is the identity) gives the identifications $M\otimes_AF\simeq V$ and $M\otimes_AL\simeq V\otimes_FL=W$. Explicitly they send $m\otimes\bar a$ to $\bar a\bar m$ and $m\otimes\ell$ to $\bar m\otimes\ell$, with inverses $\bar m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and $\bar m\otimes\ell\mapsto m\otimes\ell$. Independence of the lift follows because $(am)\otimes\ell=m\otimes a\ell=0$ for $a\in\mathfrak m$, and the formulas verify scalar linearity and both composites on generators. They carry the residue images of the $m_i$ to $m_i\otimes1$, so all basis and generator assertions, including the dimension equalities and inequalities of steps 3 and 4, hold for the stated fibres as well.
